findings.title: Production stateful asset lacks observed backup coverage
findings.observation: The asset is declared production and stateful, but no backup configuration is observed.
findings.expected_state: Production state has a tested, declared recovery mechanism.
prerequisites: Collector coverage includes the relevant backup mechanism.
findings.impact: Deletion, corruption, or compromise may cause unrecoverable service data loss.

verification.notes: Absence evidence depends on complete collector coverage; validate the missing control with the owner.

findings.remediation: Enable provider or application-consistent backups and record a restore test.

findings.title: Privileged container crosses the host isolation boundary
findings.observation: Runtime inspection reports privileged=true.
findings.expected_state: The workload has only capabilities required by its declared function.
prerequisites: Code execution in the container.
findings.impact: Container compromise can expand to host or sibling-workload control.

verification.notes: Evidence is internally consistent and no observed compensating control refutes the path.

findings.remediation: Disable privileged and grant a narrower capability or mediated service.

findings.title: Runtime network access diverges from declared infrastructure
findings.observation: Declared and observed source ranges differ for a security-sensitive port.
findings.expected_state: TCP/22 sources equal the declared set ['100.64.0.0/10'].
prerequisites: Repository declaration is current and refers to the observed asset.
findings.impact: The provider policy no longer enforces the reviewed source restriction; downstream reachability requires separate host and service evidence.

verification.notes: Evidence is internally consistent and no observed compensating control refutes the path.

findings.remediation: Reconcile the runtime firewall to reviewed IaC, then import or remove manual drift.

findings.title: SSH reachable from the public internet
findings.observation: An inbound rule admits a public source to TCP/22.
findings.expected_state: Management and data services are reachable only from declared trusted sources.
prerequisites: The rule is attached to the target and no downstream firewall blocks it.
findings.impact: An unauthenticated network peer can reach a sensitive service boundary.

verification.notes: The provider rule is attached, but listener and host-firewall evidence are incomplete; validate end-to-end reachability safely.

findings.remediation: Restrict the rule to a VPN, bastion, or explicit workload CIDR and verify host controls.

findings.title: Internet-facing server has no observed firewall control
findings.observation: A public interface exists, but neither an attached Hetzner firewall nor an observed host firewall is present.
findings.expected_state: Every public server has an independently evidenced ingress control.
findings.actual_state: Public IP present; firewall attachment and host firewall evidence absent.
prerequisites: Collector coverage includes firewall attachments and host firewall state.
findings.impact: Services that bind broadly may be reachable without a network policy boundary.

verification.notes: Absence evidence depends on complete collector coverage; validate the missing control with the owner.

findings.remediation: Attach a least-privilege Hetzner firewall or provide verified host-firewall evidence.

findings.title: Broad PostgreSQL trust authentication bypasses credentials
findings.observation: pg_hba.conf trusts a broad network range.
findings.expected_state: Remote database connections use authenticated, encrypted methods scoped to required clients.
prerequisites: A network path reaches PostgreSQL and the HBA rule is selected.
findings.impact: A reachable client can select an allowed database role without presenting a password.

verification.notes: Evidence is internally consistent and no observed compensating control refutes the path.

findings.remediation: Replace trust with scram-sha-256 or certificate authentication and scope the CIDR.

findings.title: Unexpected PostgreSQL roles hold superuser capability
findings.observation: Role inventory marks superuser roles outside the declared allowlist.
findings.expected_state: Only explicitly designated break-glass or administrative roles are superusers.
prerequisites: Ability to authenticate as one of the listed roles.
findings.impact: The roles can bypass database authorization and alter security-sensitive configuration.

verification.notes: Evidence is internally consistent and no observed compensating control refutes the path.

findings.remediation: Revoke SUPERUSER and grant the minimum object and administrative privileges.

findings.title: Redis accepts non-local clients without an authentication control
findings.observation: Broad bind, disabled protected mode, and absent ACL/password evidence coincide.
findings.expected_state: Redis is limited to trusted clients and requires a scoped ACL identity.
findings.actual_state: bind is broad; protected-mode=no; no authentication configured.
prerequisites: A network path reaches the Redis listener.
findings.impact: A client can read, alter, or destroy cached or persistent data.

verification.notes: Evidence is internally consistent and no observed compensating control refutes the path.

findings.remediation: Bind to the required interface, enable protected mode, and configure least-privilege ACLs.

findings.title: staging workload can reach prod postgres
findings.observation: A cross-environment attack-graph path contradicts an explicit isolation declaration.
findings.expected_state: staging and prod data planes are isolated.
findings.actual_state: A TCP/5432 path exists: container:stage-worker -> network:shared -> postgres:prod
prerequisites: Compromise or malicious execution on container:stage-worker.
Target service accepts the source identity.
findings.impact: Compromise of a lower-trust environment can become unauthorized database or cache access.

verification.notes: Evidence is internally consistent and no observed compensating control refutes the path.

findings.remediation: Separate environment networks and enforce target-side allowlists for the exact clients.
